sections.purpose: The Daily Protein Target is an educational screening aid that estimates a daily protein intake target, in grams per day, grams per kilogram and per meal, for healthy adults from published guidelines and trials. It is not a prescription, not a diagnosis and not individualised clinical nutrition advice.
sections.who: Adults aged 18 to 99. The tool gives no number, and asks you to speak to your clinician, if you have kidney disease or are on dialysis, have liver disease or are recovering from a serious illness, injury or surgery, or follow a diet or protein plan from a doctor or dietitian. Pregnancy and breastfeeding use the World Health Organization figures for your stage. The tool is not for children.
sections.enter:
• Age and sex, and your stage if you are pregnant or breastfeeding
  • Height and weight (metric or imperial)
  • Ethnicity (sets the healthy weight range shown to you)
  • Activity level and whether you do strength training at least twice a week
  • Your goal, how you eat and how many meals you have
  • Kidney, liver and clinician-plan questions
sections.limitations:
• Published guideline and trial figures, not individual requirements: the tool cannot see kidney function tests, protein quality, energy balance, medicines or conditions beyond the questions it asks.
  • The tool covers intakes up to 2.0 g/kg a day; that is the scope of a general tool, not a safety limit.
  • Above a healthy weight, only part of the extra weight is counted, a standard dietetic convention.

Read the medical disclaimer and when to seek urgent care.
sections.how: The tool finds the published range that fits your age, activity, strength training and goal (WHO 2007 and the US RDA; Tagawa 2021; the 2016 joint position of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics, Dietitians of Canada and the American College of Sports Medicine; the ISSN 2017 position stand and Morton 2018; Leidy 2015 and Wycherley 2012 for fat loss; PROT-AGE, ESPEN and Nunes 2022 for older adults). Where more than one applies, the range with the highest top is used, and your starting target is its middle. Pregnancy and breastfeeding use the WHO figures on their own. Engine: Lifeline Daily Protein Target engine v2. Deployed version [lld_tool_version slug="protein"].
sections.privacy: The calculation runs in your browser. Nothing you enter is stored on our servers. If you choose to email yourself the result, the e-mail is sent once and not kept; see our Privacy Policy.

sections.purpose: The Diabetes Risk Check is an educational screening aid that estimates your 10-year risk of developing type 2 diabetes from self-reported, non-laboratory inputs, and encourages a conversation with a clinician or an NHS Health Check where indicated. It does not diagnose diabetes, type 1 diabetes or any other condition.
sections.who: Adults aged 25 to 84 without a diagnosis of diabetes. Age is entered as a five-year band. Classic symptoms trigger a same-day-assessment banner; the emergency checklist suppresses the percentage and directs you to urgent care. The tool is not a diagnosis.
sections.enter:
• Age band and sex
  • Height, weight and (optionally) waist
  • Ethnicity and smoking
  • Family history and medical history
  • Current symptoms, checked separately from the score
sections.limitations:
• QDiabetes was developed using UK health records. Its accuracy in other countries has not been established.
  • The Townsend deprivation score is fixed at a neutral average, which can under- or over-state risk for individual visitors.
  • Band labels and thresholds (5.6 %, 10 %, 20 %) are interpretation cut-points chosen by Lifeline Daily.

Read the medical disclaimer and when to seek urgent care.
sections.how: The score is the published QDiabetes-2018 (Model A) algorithm, calibrated in the UK, which uses a deprivation score we hold fixed and estimates type 2 diabetes risk; symptoms are handled separately from the number. Waist-to-height ratio and the Indian Diabetes Risk Score are shown as cross-checks. Engine: QDiabetes-2018 (Model A). Deployed version [lld_tool_version slug="diabetes"].
sections.privacy: The calculation runs in your browser. Nothing you enter is stored on our servers. If you choose to email yourself the result, the e-mail is sent once and not kept; see our Privacy Policy.

healthy-weight.title: Healthy Weight Check
healthy-weight.engine: NICE NG246 BMI and waist-to-height ratio

sections.purpose: The Healthy Weight Check works out your body mass index (BMI), your waist-to-height ratio if you add your waist, and a healthy weight range for your height, with plain guidance on what they mean. It does not diagnose any condition, set a weight target or give calorie advice.
sections.who: Adults aged 18 to 99. It is not for children or teenagers, during pregnancy or while breastfeeding, or for anyone with an eating disorder; in those cases it explains why and shows no numbers. If you have lost weight without trying, it asks you to see your doctor.
sections.enter:
• Your age
  • Whether you are pregnant or breastfeeding
  • Whether you have, or have had, an eating disorder or worries about eating
  • Height and weight (metric or imperial)
  • Waist (optional), with how to measure it
  • Your family background, which sets the BMI thresholds
  • Whether you have lost weight without trying
sections.limitations:
• BMI is a screening measure, not a diagnosis. It is less reliable for older adults, very muscular people and people who have had a limb removed.
  • Measurements you enter yourself may not be exact.
  • At a BMI of 35 or more, waist-to-height ratio is not used.

Read the medical disclaimer and when to seek urgent care.
sections.how: BMI categories follow NICE guideline NG246 (2025), with lower thresholds for people of South Asian, Chinese, other Asian, Middle Eastern, Black African or African-Caribbean family background. Waist-to-height ratio bands follow the same guidance: 0.40 to 0.49 healthy, 0.50 to 0.59 increased, 0.60 or more high. Deployed version [lld_tool_version slug="healthy-weight"].
sections.privacy: The check runs in your browser. Nothing you enter is stored or sent. If you have an account with health consent, you can choose to save just your BMI and its category to your profile.

disclaimer.title: Medical Disclaimer & Urgent Care
disclaimer.content:
Screening, not diagnosis

The Lifeline Daily health tools give general information and screening estimates from published methods. A result is not a diagnosis and does not replace advice from a doctor, nurse, dietitian or pharmacist who knows your history.

When to seek urgent care

If you feel very unwell, for example vomiting, drowsiness or confusion, fast or deep breathing, chest pain, or stomach pain, get medical help today. Do not wait for a screening result.

In an emergency, call your local emergency number now, for example 999 in the UK, 911 in the US and Canada, 112 in the EU and India, or 000 in Australia. In the UK you can also call NHS 111 for urgent advice.

What the tools cannot do

The tools use only the answers you give. They cannot see your blood tests, medicines or medical history, and they are not designed for children, pregnancy-specific care beyond what each tool states, or people under specialist care for kidney or liver disease. Each tool page lists its own limitations.

Contact

Questions about these pages or the tools: contact us. Privacy: see our Privacy Policy.
